body_markdown:
Toyota traveled to SEMA 2026 to introduce five close-to-production concepts designed to keep going when the pavement ends. Grouped under the Toyota Woodland label, the concepts are united by a common design theme and off-road-ready modifications.


Finished in a 1960s-inspired color called Horizon Blue, the five concepts are based on[the RAV4](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-2026-toyota-rav4-adds-power-looks-and-gr-flair/) ,[the Grand Highlander](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2024-toyota-grand-highlander-review-un-minivan/) , the battery-electric BZ,[the Sienna](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-toyota-sienna-gets-even-smarter-for-family-hauling-duties/) , and[the Crown Signia](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-toyota-crown-signia-limited-old-name-new-look-old-soul/) , respectively. Toyota[already sells](https://www.hagerty.com/media/driving/how-minivan-overlanding-fed-my-soul/) a Woodland version of most of these vehicles (the Crown Signia is the exception), but the concepts inaugurate a new, markedly more rugged look for the trim. They all receive the same basic set of updates, including a lift kit and black-finished rally-inspired wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. Each sports black accents on the hood and roof panel and a Yakima roof basket. In contrast, the regular-production Grand Highlander Woodland looks a little tame.


Designers added several model-specific details as well. The BZ gets gray trim on the lower front bumper, for example, while the Crown Signia features rugged-looking front-end trim and a pair of additional lights.

Interior pictures haven’t been released, so we’re unsure whether the Woodland treatment extends throughout the cabin. It doesn’t sound like there are major mechanical modifications beyond the lift kit, tires, roof rack, and aesthetic tweaks. Indeed, the current Woodland models don’t include any hardcore hardware changes, either, suggesting that Toyota is and will be content to leave such things to the TRD range.


What’s next for the five Toyota Woodland concepts? Good question. Toyota says that the concepts “imagine a future where more vehicles are ready to leave the pavement behind and make the journey itself part of the story.” The five cars are relatively close to production, so we wouldn’t be surprised if they preview a new family look for an expanded Toyota Woodland range.


The five Toyota Woodland concepts will be displayed at the SEMA show that opens its doors in Las Vegas, Nevada, on November 3, 2026. They’ll share the spotlight with[the Crown Signia GT-S Performance concept](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/toyotas-crown-signia-gt-s-embraces-station-wagon-swagger/) , which gets tuning-inspired, street-oriented modifications. We will be there to bring you the latest updates straight from the show floor, so stay tuned for more.
